domain_restrictions: n is an integer with n > 1
x is a real number (or at least a value for which floor(n x) and floor(k x) are defined)
k ranges over integers from 1 to n (so division by k is valid since k is nonzero)
m is an integer satisfying 0 <= m <= n - 1
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every integer n with n > 1, define F_n on real x by F_n(x) = floor(n times x) minus the sum over integers k from 1 to n of floor(k times x) divided by k. Then for every integer m with 0 <= m <= n - 1, F_n(m divided by n) equals m minus the sum over integers k from 1 to n of floor(k times m divided by n) divided by k.
quantifier_order: For all integers n such that n > 1
For all integers m such that 0 <= m <= n - 1

variables.name: n
variables.role: global parameter in the definition of F_n

variables.name: k
variables.role: summation index in the definition of F_n

variables.name: m
variables.role: quantified argument where x is specialized to m/n

witness_dependencies: No existential witnesses are introduced; the claim is universally quantified over m with fixed n

statement_nl: Let n be an integer greater than 1, and define F_n(x) = floor(n x) - sum_{k=1}^{n} floor(k x)/k. For every integer m with 0 <= m <= n-1, F_n(m/n) = m - sum_{k=1}^{n} floor(k m/n)/k.
